verdicts.notes: Wrong event type: imFileEvent instead of imProcessCreate. GT detects LOLBin process execution with 'recycler' in the command line; System B checks FilePath instead, dropping the LOLBin process-list filter entirely.

Inverted logic. GT detects sdelete's accepteula/-s/-r/-q flag combination specifically when the binary is NOT named sdelete.exe and 'sdelete' is NOT in the command line (the renamed-binary evasion case). System B requires 'sdelete' to be PRESENT, the opposite condition.
Wrong event type: imFileEvent instead of imProcessCreate. Same underlying detection as -original; same family of error, different specific manifestation.

Correct event type and the core flag-combination check (accepteula, -s, -r, -q all required) plus the sdelete.exe filename exclusion. Missing the 'command line does not contain sdelete' exclusion, but the core technique is captured correctly.
Exact match to GT's actual active logic (the whitelist line in GT is commented out, so GT's real filter is just 'Process has rundll32.exe').
Same intent as GT; literal value 'rundll32' instead of 'rundll32.exe' is a minor literal-match risk but directionally correct.
Wrong event type (imNetworkSession instead of imWebSession), wrong field (EventResult contains 'error' instead of an HTTP 5xx status-code check), and a near-degenerate threshold (>1 vs GT's 100).
Correct event type, correct condition (HttpStatusCode >= 500), and threshold exactly matches GT's 100.
Precise match: HttpStatusCode in [500,600), per-source count, threshold 100 exactly matching GT.
Correct structure (dcount(HttpUserAgent) by source) but threshold of 1 vs GT's explicit 5 is a 5x sensitivity mismatch that materially changes detection behavior, not a minor variation.
Correct structure and threshold (>5) exactly matching GT.
HttpStatusCode==200 is an imperfect but reasonable proxy for GT's eventresult='Success' filter; core dcount/threshold structure matches GT's 5 exactly.
Clean match: HttpStatusCode==403, per-source daily count, threshold 100 exactly matching GT.

Same condition and threshold as the casual variant, but grouping adds DstUsername and SrcHostname alongside SrcIpAddr — this changes the aggregation granularity substantially (each 3-key combination must individually exceed 100, a much narrower condition than GT's per-source-IP intent).
